answer.note: I confirmed the incoming handoff's choice of B and D. I didn't open the ref files themselves. radon/complexity.py is where the ordering lives. It defines SCORE (negated complexity, so descending), LINES (block.lineno) and ALPHA (block.name), and sorted_results(blocks, order=SCORE) applies them. radon/visitors.py defines the block classes that supply the lineno, name and complexity attributes those keys read. Suggested 60-minute split: about 35 minutes on complexity.py, covering the key lambdas, sorted_results, tie-breaking and stability, and the SCORE default. About 20 minutes on visitors.py, checking that every block type has lineno and name and that nested blocks (methods, closures) behave sensibly under the sort. About 5 minutes on the CLI wiring in radon/cli/__init__.py, which maps the order string through getattr to the key function and falls back to SCORE. Skip radon/raw.py and radon/metrics.py, which don't touch block ordering.
